stem: Ridgemont Systems stored a group of subnet names in a `set(string)` variable and needs to read the second one out by position. What must happen first?

choices.text: Index the set directly with `[1]`, treating a set as already ordered the way a list is
Convert the set to a map with `tomap()`, then index it by an integer key
Convert the set to a list with `tolist()`, then index the result
Reference the set element by a string key, such as `var.names["second"]`

rationale: Sets are unordered collections with no index of their own; converting to a list with `tolist()` is exactly how Terraform's own documentation says to access an element by position. Indexing a set directly isn't supported, because Terraform doesn't assign set members a stable position the way it does list elements. Converting to a map doesn't help either, since maps are addressed by a string key, not a numeric position. A set has no named keys the way a map does, so there is nothing to reference by string key -- 'named labels' is what distinguishes a map/object, not a set.
